movimento: Em pé, com os pés paralelos e afastados na largura dos ombros, os joelhos soltos e o tronco ereto, segura a barra por cima (pegada pronada: as palmas viradas para as coxas), com as mãos um pouco mais afastadas que a largura dos ombros, logo por fora das coxas, e os braços esticados, com a barra na frente das coxas, quase encostando nelas. Sobe só os ombros, reto, em direção às orelhas, o mais alto que conseguir (pelo menos até a linha dos ombros ficar na horizontal), sem dobrar os cotovelos e sem girar (rolar) os ombros para a frente ou para trás — a barra sobe junto, rente às coxas; segura 1 segundo em cima e desce devagar até os ombros voltarem embaixo. Os ombros ficam um pouco para trás (peito aberto) e a cabeça parada, alinhada com a coluna, olhando para a frente.

cinesiologia.plano: frontal (elevação e depressão da escápula), cadeia cinética aberta
cinesiologia.articulacoes: cintura escapular: elevação da escápula e da clavícula (articulação esternoclavicular) na subida e depressão na descida, com as escápulas um pouco para trás e paradas (sem rolar); ombros (glenoumeral), cotovelos (estendidos) e punhos (retos) parados; tronco, quadril, joelhos (soltos, ~7°) e pés parados
cinesiologia.agonistas: trapézio superior (ExRx: "Target: Trapezius, Upper"; Yessis: "In the barbell shrug, only the uppermost portion of the trapezius is involved."; Ekstrom 2003: "The unilateral shoulder shrug exercise was found to produce the greatest EMG activity in the upper trapezius.")
cinesiologia.sinergistas: levantador da escápula e trapézio médio (ExRx: "Synergists: Trapezius, Middle; Levator Scapulae"); Yessis põe também o romboide entre os músculos do movimento ("This includes the rhomboid, uppermost portion of the trapezius, and the levator scapulae"; do levantador: "Because of its direct line of pull it plays an important role in the shrug movement."). No mapa do app o levantador da escápula fica embaixo do trapézio, que fica vermelho (catálogo: "Trapézio superior · elevador da escápula")
cinesiologia.estabilizadores: eretores da espinha, que seguram o tronco ereto (ExRx: "Stabilizers: Erector Spinae"); flexores dos dedos e do punho seguram a barra (pegada)
cinesiologia.fases: subida concêntrica até o ombro mais alto que der, com 1 s de pausa em cima (free-exercise-db: "hold the contraction for a second"; Yessis: "hold for one to two seconds"), e descida excêntrica devagar (ACE: "lowering slowly to the original starting position"; free-exercise-db: "Slowly return to the starting position")

free-exercise-db (yuhonas, domínio público) — Barbell Shrug (a de onde o catálogo tirou o fonte_en). https://github.com/yuhonas/free-exercise-db (exercises/Barbell_Shrug.json, lido em 11/10/2026): "Stand up straight with your feet at shoulder width as you hold a barbell with both hands in front of you using a pronated grip (palms facing the thighs). ExRx.net — Barbell Shrug (Weight Exercises › Trapezius, Upper). https://exrx.net/WeightExercises/TrapeziusUpper/BBShrug (lido em 11/10/2026 na cópia do Internet Archive de 06/02/2026: https://web.archive.org/web/20260206131420/https://exrx.net/WeightExercises/TrapeziusUpper/BBShrug; o site responde 403 direto): Preparation "Stand holding barbell with overhand or mixed grip; shoulder width or slightly wider."; Execution "Elevate shoulders as high as possible. For example, raising shoulders until slope of shoulders becomes horizontal may be considered adequate depending upon individual body structure and range of motion with lighter weight."; músculos: Target "Trapezius, Upper", Synergists "Trapezius, Middle", "Levator Scapulae", Stabilizers "Erector Spinae"

ExRx.net — Kinesiology › Exercise Errors, Shoulder Shrugs Errors (shoulder rolls). https://exrx.net/Kinesiology/Errors (cópia do Internet Archive de 04/08/2025, lida em 11/10/2026): "Rolling (horizontal movement) is nonsensical"; "Bottom line: It's only necessary to raise and lower the shoulders during shrugs."

American Council on Exercise (ACE) — Shrug (Exercise Library nº 72, "Equipment: Barbell"). https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/72/shrug/ (lido em 11/10/2026): "Hold a barbell with a palms-down grip with the hands about shoulder-width apart. Keep the knees slightly bent, the hips straight, and the back tall, and raise the shoulders directly upwards to the ears as high as possible, lowering slowly to the original starting position. (Tip: grip the bar and think about pulling the hands apart from one another and focus on only raising/lowering the shoulders - DO NOT roll the shoulders.)"

American Council on Exercise (ACE) — Standing Shrug (Exercise Library nº 75, com halteres). https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/75/standing-shrug/ (lido em 11/10/2026): "with your elbows fully extended"; "Your head and neck should be aligned with your spine."; "Exhale and slowly shrug your shoulders upward, avoiding any shoulder rotation or elbow flexion (bending). Maintain an erect torso (no arching in your low back) and neutral wrist position (wrists held straight without any bending)."

Yessis M. — The Barbbell Shrug (Dr. Yessis SportLab). https://doctoryessis.com/2013/01/01/the-barbbell-shrug/ (lido em 11/10/2026): "Assume a standing position with the feet in line with one another and approximately shoulder-width apart. Your body should be erect with the lumbar spine in its neutral (slightly arched) position."; "Your head should be directly above the shoulders in good spinal alignment and your vision focused directly in front."; "Keep the shoulders back and the chest out as much as possible."; "Hold a barbell with extended arms and with the hands slightly wider than hip-width apart. The bar should rest against your thighs."; "Inhale and hold your breath as you raise the shoulders as high as possible."; "There should be no bending in the elbow as you raise the shoulders."; "After reaching the uppermost position, hold for one to two seconds to maximize the muscular contraction."; "Exhale as you return the shoulders under control to the initial position."; "It is important that you keep the head up and look directly in front as you execute the shrug."; "The muscles involved in the shrug raise the scapula (and clavicle) directly upward with no rotation of the scapula."
